audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Samuel chapter 24, first-pass draft aligned later; compare 1 Chronicles 21
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for conflicting incitement traditions, census as military and extractive administration, Joab's objection, route and totals, David's conscience, three punishments and variants, ruler-chosen collective suffering, plague deaths, Divine relenting, angel imagery, David's command responsibility, Araunah's Jebusite land and power imbalance, payment variants, animal sacrifice, and plague cessation.

verses.restored: Anger of YHWH again burned against Israel, and YHWH incited David against them, saying, Go, count Israel and Judah.

familiar.text: And again the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel, and he moved David against them to say, Go, number Israel and Judah.

modern.text: Again the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He stirred up David against them, saying, “Go and take a census of Israel and Judah.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨סֶף֙ אַף יְהוָ֔ה לַחֲר֖וֹת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיָּ֨סֶת אֶת דָּוִ֤ד בָּהֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֵ֛ךְ מְנֵ֥ה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְאֶת יְהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: King said to Joab, commander of army who was with him, Go about through all tribes of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, and muster/count people, that I may know number of people.

familiar.text: For the king said to Joab the captain of the host, which was with him, Go now through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan even to Beersheba, and number ye the people, that I may know the number of the people.

modern.text: So the king said to Joab the commander of his army, who was with him, “Go now throughout the tribes of Israel from Dan to Beersheba and register the troops, so that I may know their number.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶל יוֹאָ֣ב שַׂר הַחַ֣יִל אֲשֶׁר אִתּ֗וֹ שֽׁוּט נָ֞א בְּכָל שִׁבְטֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִדָּן֙ וְעַד בְּאֵ֣ר שֶׁ֔בַע וּפִקְד֖וּ אֶת הָעָ֑ם וְיָ֣דַעְתִּ֔י אֵ֖ת מִסְפַּ֥ר הָעָֽם

verses.restored: Joab said to king, May YHWH your Divine add to people, however many they are, one hundred times, while eyes of my lord king see. But why does my lord king delight in this thing?

familiar.text: And Joab said unto the king, Now the LORD thy God add unto the people, how many soever they be, an hundredfold, and that the eyes of my lord the king may see it: but why doth my lord the king delight in this thing?

modern.text: But Joab replied to the king, “May the LORD your God multiply the troops a hundred times over, and may the eyes of my lord the king see it. But why does my lord the king want to do such a thing?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יוֹאָ֜ב אֶל הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וְיוֹסֵ֣ף יְהוָה֩ אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ אֶל הָעָ֜ם כָּהֵ֤ם וְכָהֵם֙ מֵאָ֣ה פְעָמִ֔ים וְעֵינֵ֥י אֲדֹנִֽי הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ רֹא֑וֹת וַאדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לָ֥מָּה חָפֵ֖ץ בַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Word of king prevailed against Joab and commanders of army. Joab and commanders went out from before king to count people of Israel.

familiar.text: Notwithstanding the king’s word prevailed against Joab, and against the captains of the host. And Joab and the captains of the host went out from the presence of the king, to number the people of Israel.

modern.text: Nevertheless, the king’s word prevailed against Joab and against the commanders of the army. So Joab and the commanders of the army departed from the presence of the king to count the troops of Israel.

original.text: וַיֶּחֱזַ֤ק דְּבַר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֶל יוֹאָ֔ב וְעַ֖ל שָׂרֵ֣י הֶחָ֑יִל וַיֵּצֵ֨א יוֹאָ֜ב וְשָׂרֵ֤י הַחַ֨יִל֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לִפְקֹ֥ד אֶת הָעָ֖ם אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: They crossed Jordan and camped at Aroer, on right side of city that is in middle of wadi of Gad, toward Jazer.

familiar.text: And they passed over Jordan, and pitched in Aroer, on the right side of the city that lieth in the midst of the river of Gad, and toward Jazer:

modern.text: They crossed the Jordan and camped near Aroer, south of the town in the middle of the valley, and proceeded toward Gad and Jazer.

original.text: וַיַּעַבְר֖וּ אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן וַיַּחֲנ֣וּ בַעֲרוֹעֵ֗ר יְמִ֥ין הָעִ֛יר אֲשֶׁ֛ר בְּתוֹךְ הַנַּ֥חַל הַגָּ֖ד וְאֶל יַעְזֵֽר

verses.restored: They came to Gilead and land of Tahtim-hodshi; they came to Dan-jaan and around toward Sidon.

familiar.text: Then they came to Gilead, and to the land of Tahtimhodshi; and they came to Danjaan, and about to Zidon,

modern.text: Then they went to Gilead and the land of Tahtim-hodshi, and on to Dan-jaan and around to Sidon.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ הַגִּלְעָ֔דָה וְאֶל אֶ֥רֶץ תַּחְתִּ֖ים חָדְשִׁ֑י וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ דָּ֣נָה יַּ֔עַן וְסָבִ֖יב אֶל צִידֽוֹן

verses.restored: They came to fortress of Tyre and all cities of Hivites and Canaanites, then went out to Negev of Judah at Beersheba.

familiar.text: And came to the strong hold of Tyre, and to all the cities of the Hivites, and of the Canaanites: and they went out to the south of Judah, even to Beersheba.

modern.text: They went toward the fortress of Tyre and all the cities of the Hivites and Canaanites. Finally, they went on to the Negev of Judah, to Beersheba.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ מִבְצַר צֹ֔ר וְכָל עָרֵ֥י הַחִוִּ֖י וְהַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֑י וַיֵּֽצְא֛וּ אֶל נֶ֥גֶב יְהוּדָ֖ה בְּאֵ֥ר שָֽׁבַע

verses.restored: They went about through all land and came to Jerusalem at end of nine months and twenty days.

familiar.text: So when they had gone through all the land, they came to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.

modern.text: At the end of nine months and twenty days, having gone through the whole land, they returned to Jerusalem.

original.text: וַיָּשֻׁ֖טוּ בְּכָל הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ מִקְצֵ֨ה תִשְׁעָ֧ה חֳדָשִׁ֛ים וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים י֖וֹם יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: Joab gave number of census of people to king: Israel was eight hundred thousand valiant men drawing sword, and men of Judah were five hundred thousand.

familiar.text: And Joab gave up the sum of the number of the people unto the king: and there were in Israel eight hundred thousand valiant men that drew the sword; and the men of Judah were five hundred thousand men.

modern.text: And Joab reported to the king the total number of the troops. In Israel there were 800,000 men of valor who drew the sword, and in Judah there were 500,000. Judgment for David’s Sin (1 Chronicles 21:7–13)

original.text: וַיִּתֵּ֥ן יוֹאָ֛ב אֶת מִסְפַּ֥ר מִפְקַד הָעָ֖ם אֶל הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַתְּהִ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל שְׁמֹנֶה֩ מֵא֨וֹת אֶ֤לֶף אִֽישׁ חַ֨יִל֙ שֹׁ֣לֵֽף חֶ֔רֶב וְאִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֔ה חֲמֵשׁ מֵא֥וֹת אֶ֖לֶף אִֽישׁ

verses.restored: David's heart struck him after he counted people. David said to YHWH, I have sinned greatly in what I did. Now, YHWH, please cause iniquity of your servant to pass, because I acted very foolishly.

familiar.text: And David’s heart smote him after that he had numbered the people. And David said unto the LORD, I have sinned greatly in that I have done: and now, I beseech thee, O LORD, take away the iniquity of thy servant; for I have done very foolishly.

modern.text: After David had numbered the troops, his conscience was stricken and he said to the LORD, “I have sinned greatly in what I have done. Now, O LORD, I beg You to take away the iniquity of Your servant, for I have acted very foolishly.”

original.text: וַיַּ֤ךְ לֵב דָּוִד֙ אֹת֔וֹ אַחֲרֵי כֵ֖ן סָפַ֣ר אֶת הָעָ֑ם וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד אֶל יְהוָ֗ה חָטָ֤אתִי מְאֹד֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔יתִי וְעַתָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה הַֽעֲבֶר נָא֙ אֶת עֲוֺ֣ן עַבְדְּךָ֔ כִּ֥י נִסְכַּ֖לְתִּי מְאֹֽד

verses.restored: When David arose in morning, word of YHWH came to prophet Gad, seer of David, saying,

familiar.text: For when David was up in the morning, the word of the LORD came unto the prophet Gad, David’s seer, saying,

modern.text: When David got up in the morning, a revelation from the LORD had come to Gad the prophet, David’s seer:

original.text: וַיָּ֥קָם דָּוִ֖ד בַּבֹּ֑קֶר וּדְבַר יְהוָ֗ה הָיָה֙ אֶל גָּ֣ד הַנָּבִ֔יא חֹזֵ֥ה דָוִ֖ד לֵאמֹֽר

verses.restored: Go and speak to David: Thus says YHWH, Three things I am laying before you; choose one of them, and I will do it to you.

familiar.text: Go and say unto David, Thus saith the LORD, I offer thee three things; choose thee one of them, that I may do it unto thee.

modern.text: “Go and tell David that this is what the LORD says: ‘I am offering you three options. Choose one of them, and I will carry it out against you.’”

original.text: הָל֞וֹךְ וְדִבַּרְתָּ֣ אֶל דָּוִ֗ד כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שָׁלֹ֕שׁ אָנֹכִ֖י נוֹטֵ֣ל עָלֶ֑יךָ בְּחַר לְךָ֥ אַֽחַת מֵהֶ֖ם וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂה לָּֽךְ

verses.restored: Gad came to David, told him, and said: Shall seven years/three years of famine come to you in your land, or will you flee three months before your adversaries while they pursue you, or shall there be three days of plague in your land? Now know and see what word I shall return to one who sent me.

familiar.text: So Gad came to David, and told him, and said unto him, Shall seven years of famine come unto thee in thy land? or wilt thou flee three months before thine enemies, while they pursue thee? or that there be three days’ pestilence in thy land? now advise, and see what answer I shall return to him that sent me.

modern.text: So Gad went and said to David, “Do you choose to endure three years of famine in your land, three months of fleeing the pursuit of your enemies, or three days of plague upon your land? Now then, think it over and decide how I should reply to Him who sent me.”

original.text: וַיָּבֹא גָ֥ד אֶל דָּוִ֖ד וַיַּגֶּד ל֑וֹ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֡וֹ הֲתָב֣וֹא לְךָ֣ שֶֽׁבַע שָׁנִ֣ים רָעָ֣ב בְּאַרְצֶ֡ךָ אִם שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה חֳ֠דָשִׁים נֻסְךָ֨ לִפְנֵֽי צָרֶ֜יךָ וְה֣וּא רֹדְפֶ֗ךָ וְאִם הֱ֠יוֹת שְׁלֹ֨שֶׁת יָמִ֥ים דֶּ֨בֶר֙ בְּאַרְצֶ֔ךָ עַתָּה֙ דַּ֣ע וּרְאֵ֔ה מָה אָשִׁ֥יב שֹׁלְחִ֖י דָּבָֽר

verses.restored: David said to Gad, I am greatly distressed. Let us fall into hand of YHWH, because YHWH's mercies are many, but let me not fall into hand of humanity.

familiar.text: And David said unto Gad, I am in a great strait: let us fall now into the hand of the LORD; for his mercies are great: and let me not fall into the hand of man.

modern.text: David answered Gad, “I am deeply distressed. Please, let us fall into the hand of the LORD, for His mercies are great; but do not let me fall into the hands of men.” A Plague on Israel (1 Chronicles 21:14–17)

original.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר דָּוִ֛ד אֶל גָּ֖ד צַר לִ֣י מְאֹ֑ד נִפְּלָה נָּ֤א בְיַד יְהוָה֙ כִּֽי רַבִּ֣ים רחמו וּבְיַד אָדָ֖ם אַל אֶפֹּֽלָה

verses.restored: YHWH gave plague in Israel from morning until appointed time. From people, from Dan to Beersheba, seventy thousand men died.

familiar.text: So the LORD sent a pestilence upon Israel from the morning even to the time appointed: and there died of the people from Dan even to Beersheba seventy thousand men.

modern.text: So the LORD sent a plague upon Israel from that morning until the appointed time, and seventy thousand of the people from Dan to Beersheba died.

original.text: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן יְהוָ֥ה דֶּ֨בֶר֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מֵהַבֹּ֖קֶר וְעַד עֵ֣ת מוֹעֵ֑ד וַיָּ֣מָת מִן הָעָ֗ם מִדָּן֙ וְעַד בְּאֵ֣ר שֶׁ֔בַע שִׁבְעִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף אִֽישׁ

verses.restored: Angel stretched hand toward Jerusalem to destroy it, but YHWH relented concerning evil and said to angel destroying among people, Enough; now release your hand. Angel of YHWH was by threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

familiar.text: And when the angel stretched out his hand upon Jerusalem to destroy it, the LORD repented him of the evil, and said to the angel that destroyed the people, It is enough: stay now thine hand. And the angel of the LORD was by the threshingplace of Araunah the Jebusite.

modern.text: But when the angel stretched out his hand to destroy Jerusalem, the LORD relented from the calamity and said to the angel who was destroying the people, “Enough! Withdraw your hand now!” At that time the angel of the LORD was by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ יָד֨וֹ הַמַּלְאָ֥ךְ יְרֽוּשָׁלִַם֮ לְשַׁחֲתָהּ֒ וַיִּנָּ֤חֶם יְהוָה֙ אֶל הָ֣רָעָ֔ה וַ֠יֹּאמֶר לַמַּלְאָ֞ךְ הַמַּשְׁחִ֤ית בָּעָם֙ רַ֔ב עַתָּ֖ה הֶ֣רֶף יָדֶ֑ךָ וּמַלְאַ֤ךְ יְהוָה֙ הָיָ֔ה עִם גֹּ֖רֶן האורנה הַיְבֻסִֽי

verses.restored: David spoke to YHWH when he saw angel striking people and said, Look, I sinned and I acted perversely, but these sheep—what did they do? Please let your hand be against me and against house of my father.

familiar.text: And David spake unto the LORD when he saw the angel that smote the people, and said, Lo, I have sinned, and I have done wickedly: but these sheep, what have they done? let thine hand, I pray thee, be against me, and against my father’s house.

modern.text: When David saw the angel striking down the people, he said to the LORD, “Surely I, the shepherd, have sinned and acted wickedly. But these sheep, what have they done? Please, let Your hand fall upon me and my father’s house.” David Builds an Altar (1 Chronicles 21:18–30)

original.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ דָּוִ֨ד אֶל יְהוָ֜ה בִּרְאֹת֣וֹ אֶֽת הַמַּלְאָ֣ךְ הַמַּכֶּ֣ה בָעָ֗ם וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֤י חָטָ֨אתִי֙ וְאָנֹכִ֣י הֶעֱוֵ֔יתִי וְאֵ֥לֶּה הַצֹּ֖אן מֶ֣ה עָשׂ֑וּ תְּהִ֨י נָ֥א יָדְךָ֛ בִּ֖י וּבְבֵ֥ית אָבִֽי

verses.restored: Gad came to David that day and said to him, Go up; raise for YHWH an altar at threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

familiar.text: And Gad came that day to David, and said unto him, Go up, rear an altar unto the LORD in the threshingfloor of Araunah the Jebusite.

modern.text: And that day Gad came to David and said to him, “Go up and build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.”

original.text: וַיָּבֹא גָ֥ד אֶל דָּוִ֖ד בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ עֲלֵה֙ הָקֵ֤ם לַֽיהוָה֙ מִזְבֵּ֔חַ בְּגֹ֖רֶן ארניה הַיְבֻסִֽי

verses.restored: David went up according to word of Gad, as YHWH commanded.

familiar.text: And David, according to the saying of Gad, went up as the LORD commanded.

modern.text: So David went up at the word of Gad, just as the LORD had commanded.

original.text: וַיַּ֤עַל דָּוִד֙ כִּדְבַר גָּ֔ד כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Araunah looked and saw king and his servants crossing toward him. Araunah went out and bowed to king, his face to ground.

familiar.text: And Araunah looked, and saw the king and his servants coming on toward him: and Araunah went out, and bowed himself before the king on his face upon the ground.

modern.text: When Araunah looked out and saw the king and his servants coming toward him, he went out and bowed facedown before the king.

original.text: וַיַּשְׁקֵ֣ף אֲרַ֗וְנָה וַיַּ֤רְא אֶת הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ וְאֶת עֲבָדָ֔יו עֹבְרִ֖ים עָלָ֑יו וַיֵּצֵ֣א אֲרַ֔וְנָה וַיִּשְׁתַּ֧חוּ לַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אַפָּ֖יו אָֽרְצָה

verses.restored: Araunah said, Why has my lord king come to his servant? David said, To buy threshing floor from you, to build altar to YHWH, so plague may be restrained from people.

familiar.text: And Araunah said, Wherefore is my lord the king come to his servant? And David said, To buy the threshingfloor of thee, to build an altar unto the LORD, that the plague may be stayed from the people.

modern.text: “Why has my lord the king come to his servant?” Araunah said. “To buy your threshing floor,” David replied, “that I may build an altar to the LORD, so that the plague upon the people may be halted.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲרַ֔וְנָה מַדּ֛וּעַ בָּ֥א אֲדֹנִֽי הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל עַבְדּ֑וֹ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד לִקְנ֧וֹת מֵעִמְּךָ֣ אֶת הַגֹּ֗רֶן לִבְנ֤וֹת מִזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וְתֵעָצַ֥ר הַמַּגֵּפָ֖ה מֵעַ֥ל הָעָֽם

verses.restored: Araunah said to David, Let my lord king take and offer what is good in his eyes. Look, cattle for burnt offering, and threshing sledges and equipment/yokes of cattle for wood.

familiar.text: And Araunah said unto David, Let my lord the king take and offer up what seemeth good unto him: behold, here be oxen for burnt sacrifice, and threshing instruments and other instruments of the oxen for wood.

modern.text: Araunah said to David, “My lord the king may take whatever seems good and offer it up. Here are the oxen for a burnt offering and the threshing sledges and ox yokes for the wood.

verses.restored: King said to Araunah, No, but buying, I will buy it from you for a price. I will not offer to YHWH my Divine burnt offerings that cost me nothing. David bought threshing floor and cattle for fifty silver shekels.

familiar.text: And the king said unto Araunah, Nay; but I will surely buy it of thee at a price: neither will I offer burnt offerings unto the LORD my God of that which doth cost me nothing. So David bought the threshingfloor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.

modern.text: “No,” replied the king, “I insist on paying a price, for I will not offer to the LORD my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing.” So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.

verses.restored: David built there an altar to YHWH and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. YHWH was entreated for land, and plague was restrained from Israel.

familiar.text: And David built there an altar unto the LORD, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. So the LORD was intreated for the land, and the plague was stayed from Israel.

modern.text: And there he built an altar to the LORD and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. Then the LORD answered the prayers on behalf of the land, and the plague upon Israel was halted.

translation_notes: Verse 1 attributes the incitement to YHWH, while 1 Chronicles 21 attributes it to an adversary/Satan. The contradiction must remain visible and prevents a single simplistic doctrine of Divine causation.
Counting people is not inherently sinful. In context the census concerns military capacity, royal reach, conscription, taxation, and extraction; Joab's objection suggests the king's purpose matters.
The totals differ from Chronicles and are logistically difficult. Ancient census figures are theological and political data, not precise modern statistics.
David confesses after the count, but the offered consequences fall primarily upon the population. A ruler's sin must not ethically authorize punishment of civilians.
The famine option reads seven years in the Masoretic Text and three in several ancient witnesses and Chronicles. The variant must be preserved.
David chooses based on Divine mercy, yet seventy thousand other people die. The narrative's collective-punishment theology is morally difficult and cannot become a model for justice.
Plague language must never be used to claim modern epidemics are Divine punishment or that victims deserve disease.
YHWH relents and stops the angel, which places mercy and cessation inside the story rather than treating maximal destruction as inevitable.
David finally names command responsibility: he sinned and the people did not. Calling them sheep reflects royal paternalism; they remain persons, households, and communities.
Araunah is Jebusite, a member of the population whose city David conquered. His offer occurs before a king accompanied by servants during emergency, creating severe power imbalance.
David's payment matters, but later temple and land traditions may not use this purchase to justify displacement, conquest, or modern territorial claims.
Chronicles gives a different price—six hundred gold shekels—for the place. The land-price traditions must not be harmonized invisibly.
Animals are killed in sacrifice. Plague cessation must not be interpreted as proof that blood payment purchases Divine forgiveness.
safety_note: Maximum safeguards: Do not blame epidemics on sin, punish populations for rulers, or treat death totals as acceptable collateral for spiritual lessons. Do not use Araunah's emergency transaction for land entitlement. Center Joab's objection, civilian deaths, Divine relenting, David's admission of responsibility, and the urgent stopping of harm.
